name: Red Dog High Card Pool
description: Red Dog High Card Pool is a one-card Indian Poker variant. Each player is dealt one card and holds it to the forehead without looking, so opponents can see it. After a round of poker betting, the highest card among those who stayed in wins the pot; ties split the pot.

overview.description: Red Dog High Card Pool is a one-card Indian Poker variant. Each player is dealt one card and holds it to the forehead without looking, so opponents can see it. After a round of poker betting, the highest card among those who stayed in wins the pot; ties split the pot.

history.origins: Indian Poker has nothing to do with India; the name comes from the visual of cards held to the forehead, resembling a Native American headdress or war bonnet. The one-card version is the most basic and presumably the original form: players ante, receive one card each, hold it to the forehead without looking, then bet in a round of poker betting; highest card wins the pot. It is documented among poker variants as a US-origin party game.
timeline: 20th century: One-card variant with cards held to forehead; name from Native American headdress visual.

setup.dealing: One card each face down; players pick up without looking and hold to forehead so others can see the card.

rules.objective: Win the pot by having the highest card among players who did not fold at showdown; if tied, split the pot.
rules.gameplay: Each player is dealt one card face down. Without looking, players hold the card to their forehead so all other players can see it. A round of poker betting follows (fold, check, bet, call, raise). After betting, remaining players showdown. The highest card wins the pot; ties split the pot. There is no suit order for breaking ties.
keyRules: One card each, held to forehead facing outward so others see it; players do not look at their own card.
Players ante, then a round of poker betting.
Highest card at showdown wins the pot; ties split the pot; no suit order.

scoring.winCondition: Highest card among players who did not fold wins the pot; ties split the pot.
